about.title: A community of people protecting lives.
about.description: Meet Kin Felina and learn about our commitment to animal welfare and community life in Sorbas.
about.intro: Kin Felina was founded to support community cats and the people who live alongside them. Our work is grounded in respect, prevention and responsibility.

values.title: Animal welfare
values.text: Food, care, shelter and ongoing support for the cats in our colonies.

values.title: Ethical management
values.text: We promote responsible, sustainable action to help people and cats live well together.

values.title: Community
values.text: We work with local residents and volunteers to build lasting solutions.

about.storyText: Kin Felina's work began on the ground in 2023, alongside the implementation of Law 7/2023. The first actions took place in Los Molinos and several parts of Sorbas town, then expanded to Moras and other communities across the municipality. The association was formally established on 1 April 2026 to give continuity, structure and coordination capacity to that voluntary work.
about.territoryTitle: A territory that needs a network
about.territoryText: Sorbas covers approximately 249 km², has fewer than 3,000 inhabitants and includes around forty villages, hamlets, cortijadas and dispersed settlements. Long distances, an ageing population and limited specialist services require a model adapted to rural life.
about.networkText: Kin Felina aims to connect residents, carers, volunteers, veterinary professionals, collaborating property owners and public administrations. The goal is to progressively map, census and monitor colonies across the whole municipality.

philosophy.title: Belonging to a shared world.
philosophy.description: The KIN idea: a reflection on belonging, care and the relationships between all living beings.
philosophy.intro: KIN FELINA begins with cats and with the people who care for them. But KIN expresses something broader: care begins when we recognise that we are connected.

sections.title: How far does our sense of belonging extend?
sections.text: Kin is a simple English word. It speaks of close relations, of those we consider part of our circle. At KIN FELINA, the idea goes beyond family or biological relatedness. It invites us to ask who shares our world and what connects us to other living beings.
sections.aside: Life is never entirely isolated. We care, depend, share and are transformed by what we are connected to.

sections.title: From family to relationship
sections.text: Marshall Sahlins described kinship as a mutuality of being: a form of belonging in which we participate in one another's existence. What happens to one person can deeply affect another. This idea also helps us understand the relationship between people, cats, territory and community.
sections.aside: Belonging is not only about sharing an origin. It is also about participating in one another's lives.

sections.title: A multispecies perspective
sections.text: A multispecies perspective questions the assumption that human beings inhabit a world separate from the rest of life. It does not erase differences between species or claim that all beings are the same. It asks us to notice the worlds we create together and the relationships on which we depend.
sections.aside: Interdependence · care · coexistence · reciprocity · belonging · responsibility

philosophy.closingText: This is why KIN FELINA is not simply a structure that acts upon animals. It is a way of connecting people who are currently working in isolation, recognising those who are already caring and creating collaboration where there has been fragmentation.
philosophy.question: Who are we willing to recognise as part of our shared world?
references: Sahlins, Marshall (2013), What Kinship Is—and Is Not.
Strang, Veronica (2023), Living kindness: Re-imagining kinship for a more humane future.
Nathan, Vetri (2026), Our Multispecies Futures: Control, Care and Kinship in a Transformed World.

colonies.contextTitle: Managing colonies across a dispersed municipality
colonies.contextText: In Sorbas, colonies are spread across the town and numerous villages and hamlets. Ethical management requires more than neutering: it also means identifying animals, monitoring their condition, coordinating carers, ensuring veterinary support and keeping basic records of each intervention.
colonies.programText: Sorbas Town Council began preparing its Municipal Community Cat Colony Management Programme in 2024 and started implementing CER actions at the end of 2025. Kin Felina welcomes this progress and works to strengthen the areas that need continuity: health monitoring, feeding, logistics, coordination and support for the people already caring for colonies.
colonies.logisticsText: The association has access to a plot and a small storage space next to one of the main colonies in Moras. It is not intended as a shelter, but as support infrastructure for storing food and handling equipment, organising carriers and recovery cages, and enabling short-term veterinary recovery.
